name: spec-truth
body: The target-truth content of a durable spec statement: what is, or what needs to become true. A tier-1–3 node states a positive, affirmative definition of what is in the present tense; a node this change-set delivers reads as already true after merge. The wording states a truth that holds at every moment — time-relative wording that ages (`today`, `now`, `currently`, `no longer`, `was`, `previously`) is a blocked form, because a statement true only at one moment is either the target truth or it belongs in git history, and a reviewer treats such wording as blocking history content whose fix is to rewrite it as what is. A node carries at most one note, and that note deepens the understanding of what is; a note details exactly one node and never another note — the binary refuses a `Note`→`Note` `details` edge at write time. A replaced statement is updated or removed, never annotated. Materializing a source spec or reconciling to an implementation rewrites the nodes to what is and leaves no provenance trail — git history, not the spec, describes the past.
